Definition
In this lesson, you will learn how a computer performs addition and subtraction.
INTRODUCTIONM
The arithmetic processing is accomplished in the Central Processing Unit or CPU.
CPU arithmetic capabilities are of prime importance since the processing of data almost always involves arithmetic.

Additionally, this lesson introduces the way in which binary addition and subtraction operations alter the status of the flag register. This is important because some arithmetic operations use the contents of the flag register as a factor in their calculations.....
Let's begin the lesson on 8086 ADDITION AND SUBTRACTION...................
LESSON MENU
ADDITION & SUBTRACTION INSTRUCTIONS
The ADD instruction can add a single byte hexadecimal number to another single byte hexadecimal number.
DISCUSSION
It can also add a hexadeximal word (two bytes) to another hexadecimal word.
The SUBTRACT instruction can subtract a single byte hexadecimal number from another single byte hexadecimal number.
It can also subtract a hexadecimal word (two bytes) from another hexadecimal word.r..umber.r..

The numbers that are added or subtracted can be from the contents of the accumulator, another register, the contents of a storage location in memory, or the immediate operand (data) contained in the instruction.
When adding or subtracting one register to or from another register, the Opcode identifies the two registers.
The instructions CANNOT add or subtract one memory location to or from another memory location.
You can only add or subtract a memory location to or from a register.
The location of the memory address is located in the SI, DI, BP or BX register.
Also, the instructions CANNOT add or subtract data to or from data...
Data must be added or subtracted from either a register or memory location.
As before, the memory address is located in the SI, DI, BP or BX register.

The addition or subtraction sets the carry flag if an overflow or borrow occurs, otherwise the carry flag is reset. There are two instruction codes used for each arithmetic function.

The first addition instruction is ADD. For example, this Opcode will add Register BX to the accumulator (Register AX). GRAPHICS TEXT)Code Mnemonic Pseudocode 03 C3 ADD AX, BX Add Register BX to Register AX
03 C3 ADD AX, BX Add Register BX to Register AX
This instruction takes the contents of the BX register and adds them to the AX register.
Remember, there are other Opcodes used for adding other registers, memory locations to registers, data to registers and data to memory.
The second instruction is called Add With Carry.GRAPHICS TEXT) Code Mnemonic Pseudocode 13 C3 ADC AX, BX Add Register BX to Register AX plus 1 if cf is set.
13 C3 ADC AX, BX Add Register BX to Register AX plus 1 if CF is set.
This instruction adds the contents of register BX to the contents of register AX and adds a 1 to the result if the carry flag is set.
This ADC instruction is important during double precision addition, or adding two bytes or words. The carry from the first byte or word addition must be used in the second byte or word addition...
Remember, there are other Opcodes used for Adding With Carry when adding registers, a memory location to a register, or data to a register or memory location.ion.
Now, let's look at the two subtract instructions...........
The first subtraction instruction is used to subtract the contents of a register for the accumulator (AX Register).
2B C3 SUB AX, BX Subtract Register BX from Register AX. s 1 if cf is set.
This instruction takes the contents of the BX register and subtracts them from the AX register.
Remember, there are other Opcodes for subtracting other registers, memory locations and data from memory.
The second subtract instruction is Subtract With Borrow.
1B C3 SBB AX, BX Subtract BX from AX and subtract 1 from result if CF is set.
This instruction subtracts the contents of register BX from the contents of register AX and subtracts a 1 from the results if the carry flag (borrow) is set.

This SBB instruction is important during double precision subtraction, or subtracting two bytes or words. The borrow from the first byte or word subtraction must be used in the second byte or word subtraction...
Again, remember there are other Opcodes for subtracting with carry from other registers, a memory location from a register or data from a register or memory location.
